summary:
LUNA NAV (Lunar Landing Site Navigator) is an advanced web-based decision-support dashboard developed for NASA’s Artemis lunar South Pole missions. Built using React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Recharts, LUNA NAV solves the critical mission-planning dilemma of balancing solar power availability against Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows in extreme south polar terrain.

The platform integrates high-precision ephemeris calculations from the NASA JPL Horizons API and topographic parameters from Moon Trek and LRO LOLA DEMs. It features an interactive stereographic polar map, a custom 3D horizon sky dome simulator, and a multi-scenario trade study engine. By evaluating lighting fractions, thermal survival constraints, and communication blackout risks, LUNA NAV outputs an explainable 0–100 Mission Readiness score.   

This tool is vital because it transforms complex orbital mechanics and terrain masking into an intuitive interface, enabling engineers to make data-driven, risk-mitigated landing site selections for lunar exploration.
details:
Project Details: LUNA NAV (Lunar Landing Site Navigator)

1. What It Does & How It Works

LUNA NAV is an advanced, web-based decision-support and ephemeris simulation dashboard built for NASA’s Artemis lunar South Pole missions. It solves the critical mission-planning challenge of balancing solar power availability against Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows in extreme polar terrain.

  • Site Selection & Mapping: Users can explore an interactive stereographic polar map covering the lunar South Pole (84∘S84^\circ\text{S}84∘S to 90∘S90^\circ\text{S}90∘S) to select official Artemis candidate landing regions (such as Shackleton Crater Rim and Nobile Crater Rim) or input custom coordinates.
  • Ephemeris Engine: The platform queries the NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris API in real time (coord@301, airless apparent mode) to compute high-precision topocentric Sun and Earth elevation and azimuth vectors.
  • 3D Horizon Simulation: Utilizing Three.js, LUNA NAV renders an interactive 3D sky dome simulator that visually tracks the topocentric motion of celestial bodies relative to local crater-rim topography.
  • Telemetry & Trade Studies: High-performance Recharts graphs track continuous illumination curves, solar energy harvest estimates (kWh\text{kWh}kWh for vertical mast arrays), and horizon-crossing events, feeding into an automated multi-scenario trade-study engine that outputs an explainable 0–100 Mission Readiness Score.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Mitigating Mission Risks: Prevents landers and rovers from straying into Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) where temperatures plunge below −200∘C-200^\circ\text{C}−200∘C and solar power drops to zero.
  • Securing Continuous Telemetry: Prevents communication blackouts caused by lunar libration and crater-rim blocking by mapping stable Direct-to-Earth (DTE) windows.
  • Democratizing Aerospace Planning: Transforms complex orbital mechanics into a fast, browser-based, interactive tool, empowering student researchers, mission planners, and engineers to run rapid trade studies and justify multi-billion-dollar landing site selections.

3. Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Core Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES6+), React, Vite, Tailwind CSS.
  • Visualization & 3D Graphics: Three.js (3D horizon sky dome simulator), Recharts (time-series telemetry and elevation curves), Lucide React (UI icons).
  • APIs & Planetary Datasets: NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris API, NASA Moon Trek, ASU Quickmap, and LRO LOLA South Pole DEMs.
  • Development Environment: Git/GitHub for version control and collaborative code management.

4. Creativity & Design Factors Considered

  • Bridging Math and Usability: Traditional aerospace tools are complex, heavy desktop applications. LUNA NAV brings high-precision astrodynamics into a sleek, real-time, browser-based control-room dashboard.
  • Multi-Criteria Trade Studies: Rather than looking at sunlight or communication in isolation, the team designed a weighted Mission Assessment Engine that evaluates competing survival constraints simultaneously, providing side-by-side comparative overlays (Scenario Alpha vs. Scenario Beta).
  • Topographic Awareness: Careful attention was given to modeling shallow solar grazing rays (0∘–7∘0^\circ\text{–}7^\circ0∘–7∘) and airless geometric horizons, ensuring the analytical model reflects real lunar South Pole operational constraints.
